chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The cross-legged posture is the encirclement of the Arabs.'

key_terms.الِاحْتِبَاءُ: A posture of sitting with legs folded or cross-legged, often associated with humility or traditional Arab custom.
key_terms.الْعَرَبِ: The Arabs, referring to the people of the Arabian Peninsula and their cultural customs.
key_terms.حِيطَانُ: Encirclement, encompassing, or distinctive characteristic; here used metaphorically to denote a defining trait.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cross-legged posture (al-ihbā) in Arab culture according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, identifies 'al-ihbā' (sitting with legs folded) as 'ḥiṭān al-ʿArab' (the enclosure/boundary of the Arabs), signifying it as a defining cultural marker of Arab identity and modesty in social gatherings. Scholars interpret 'ḥiṭān' metaphorically as a protective boundary that preserves dignity and distinguishes Arab custom from other postures, linking physical demeanor to social and religious propriety.
